lesson.menu_desc: Offer, recommend and share at a dinner table abroad -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Dining with Friends
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marlene Landucci | Lesson 23 -- Dining with Friends
lesson.grammar_point: would you like ...? for offers + you should try ... for recommendations

listenings.text: Hi Marlene, this is Carla. I am calling about dinner tomorrow. We have a table for six people at eight o'clock, at the little trattoria near the river. I know this place very well, so let me help you. You should try the tomato bread. It is the best appetizer on the menu, and it is perfect to share with the whole table. For the main course, I recommend the grilled fish. My sister is vegetarian, so she always takes the mushroom pasta, and she says it is wonderful. At the end we always split the bill, so please do not worry about money. Would you like me to pick you up at your hotel at half past seven? Send me a message tonight. See you tomorrow.

Good evening, and welcome to the trattoria. Let me tell you about tonight. Our appetizer of the day is warm bread with tomato and olive oil, and it comes in a big plate for the table, so you can share it. For the main course we have two specials. The first is grilled fish with lemon, and I recommend it to everybody. The second is mushroom pasta, and it is completely vegetarian. If you would like a dessert, the lemon cake is made here every morning. When you finish, we can bring one bill for the table or we can split it. Please call me if you need anything. Enjoy your evening.

extra_audio.text: First, a friend offers you something to drink and you answer. Then you look at the menu and you ask the friend what is good here. Next, the friend recommends a dish and you order the appetizer and the main course. After that, you share the appetizer with the whole table. Finally, you ask for the bill and everybody splits it.
